title: GARG-AML against Smurfing: A Scalable and Interpretable Graph-Based Framework for Anti-Money Laundering
abstract: arXiv:2506.04292v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Money laundering, a global problem estimated to account for 2%-5% of the global GDP, required regulators to enforce stringent rules on financial institutions to combat it. One prominent laundering method, called smurfing, relies on breaking up transactions into smaller amounts to evade detection. Given the complexity of laundering schemes, involving numerous transactions across multiple parties, network analytics is an important tool for anti-money laundering. However, recent advances in network analytics have leaned heavily on black-box network embedding methods, limiting their utility in businesses. To address the specific nature of smurfing and banks' operational requirements, this paper introduces GARG-AML, a novel graph-based method that quantifies smurfing risk through a single interpretable metric derived from the structure of the second-order transaction network. translated_title: GARG-AML对抗分拆洗钱：一个可扩展且可解释的基于图的反洗钱框架
translated_abstract: 洗钱是一个全球性问题，据估计占全球GDP的2%-5%，这促使监管机构对金融机构实施严格规定以打击洗钱行为。一种典型的洗钱手段被称为“分拆洗钱”，即通过将交易拆分成较小金额来逃避检测。鉴于洗钱方案的复杂性——涉及多方之间的大量交易——网络分析成为反洗钱的重要工具。然而，近年来网络分析领域的进展严重依赖黑盒网络嵌入方法，限制了其在实际业务中的应用。为应对分拆洗钱的特殊性质以及银行的运营要求，本文提出了GARG-AML，这是一种新颖的基于图的方法，通过从二阶交易网络结构中导出的单一可解释指标来量化分拆洗钱风险。与传统方法不同，GARG-AML在性能与可解释性之间取得了平衡
tldr: 本文提出GARG-AML框架，通过从二阶交易网络结构中提取的单一可解释指标量化分拆洗钱风险，在保持可扩展性的同时兼顾了可解释性，克服了黑盒网络嵌入方法在实际银行业务中的局限。
en_tdlr: GARG-AML is a scalable and interpretable graph-based framework that quantifies smurfing risk through a single interpretable metric derived from the second-order transaction network structure, balancing detection performance with explainability for real-world anti-money laundering operations.
